job.system:
You are the AI assistant for Capitol Policy Review. Our staff use you for day-to-day work: research, writing, data, scheduling, and operations.

About us: Capitol Policy Review (CPR) is a nonpartisan, nonprofit newsroom based in Washington, DC, covering science and technology legislation in Congress. We publish explainers, vote trackers, and a weekly newsletter read by policy professionals. We do not take positions on legislation; our goal is accurate, fair, and useful coverage.

Current focus: One of our biggest stories this fall is S. 2817, the Deep Seabed Mining Prohibition Act. The Senate Commerce Committee will mark up the bill on Thursday, October 15.

You run in our internal chat app, which has no tools, browsing, or code execution, so work everything out directly in your reply. Staff rely on your work, so be accurate and thorough.

- Every meeting is 30 minutes and starts on the hour or at :15, :30, or :45.

- Team A is available 9:00–17:00 both days. Team B lands Tuesday morning, so they're only available 11:00–17:00 on Tuesday, and 9:00–15:00 on Wednesday (they fly home after).
- Walking times. Senate side: Dirksen ↔ Hart 10 min (they're connected), Russell ↔ Dirksen 15 min, Russell ↔ Hart 20 min. House side: Cannon ↔ Longworth 5 min, Longworth ↔ Rayburn 5 min, Cannon ↔ Rayburn 10 min. Any Senate building ↔ any House building: 25 min. Same building: no travel time. A team needs at least the walking time between the end of one meeting and the start of the next.
- Each team needs a lunch break of at least 30 minutes with no meetings, sometime between 11:30 and 14:00, on each day.
- One meeting per office is plenty.

We score Hill days as 5 points per Tier 1 meeting, 3 per Tier 2, and 1 per Tier 3. Please find the schedule with the most points. We probably can't fit everyone in.

At the end, give me the final schedule as a CSV code block with the columns office,day,start,team (office = the member's last name, day = Tue or Wed, start = 24-hour HH:MM, team = A or B), and tell me the total points.

# Hill days schedule — Oct 13–14 (S. 2817 / H.R. 5521 preview)

**Bottom line: 24 meetings, 76 points** (out of a theoretical 94 if all 36 offices fit). All eight Tier 1 offices are covered, 10 of 13 Tier 2, and 5 of 15 Tier 3.

## Key constraints that shaped this

- **The Tier 1 crunch is Wednesday 13:00–14:15.** Okafor (Hart 13:00–14:00), Fischer (Cannon 13:00–13:45), and Doyle (Russell, 13:45 only) can't all be done Wednesday with two teams — whoever finishes Okafor or Fischer at 13:30 can't walk to Russell by 13:45. So one of Okafor/Fischer has to move to Tuesday. Okafor on Tuesday is the better move: Team A can chain Rourke → Okafor → Alvarez → Lund (Dirksen/Hart, short walks) for 16 points before lunch.
- **Rourke is Tuesday-morning only (Team A only, since B lands late).** That rules out Montoya's Tuesday slot and Sandoval's Tuesday slot for A; Montoya moves to Wednesday, Sandoval doesn't fit anywhere (its Wednesday slot collides with Montoya/Gallagher for both teams).
- **Barlow + Gallagher** both need the 10:00–11:45 Wednesday window in Dirksen/Hart; one team does Barlow 10:30 → Gallagher 11:15 and picks up Lindqvist and Stein beforehand.
- **Team B's Wednesday 15:00 departure** means Pruitt (Cannon 15:00) and Pike (Russell 14:45) are Team A only. A takes the Cannon/Rayburn cluster (Fischer, Abernathy, Pruitt); B takes Russell (Doyle, Crowe).
- **Lindqvist** fits either day; Wednesday is better (it anchors B's Senate morning, and it lets B pick up Mercer on Tuesday instead).

## Rule check

- Every meeting is 30 minutes, starts on a quarter-hour, and sits entirely inside the office's window.
- Team B's first Tuesday meeting is 11:15; its last Wednesday meeting ends 14:45.
- Walking times all hold (tightest: B's Dirksen→Russell at 9:30→9:45 Wed and 15:15→15:30 Tue, exactly 15 min; A's Hart→Dirksen 11:15→11:30 Tue, 10 min used of 15 available; A's Longworth→Cannon→Rayburn hops Wed, 5–10 min).
- Lunches: Tue A 12:00–13:30, Tue B 12:30–14:00, Wed A 12:00–13:00, Wed B 11:45–13:45 — all ≥30 min inside 11:30–14:00.
- One meeting per office.

## Who we don't get to

Tier 2 (3 pts each): **Nakamura** (Tue 10:45 Rayburn only — A is in Hart with Okafor), **Sandoval** (Tue slot collides with Rourke; Wed slot collides with Montoya/Gallagher), **Brooks** (Wed afternoon Hart — both teams are tied up in Russell/Cannon then).
Tier 3: Grant, Park, Vasquez, Kowalski, Osei, Pike, Haddad, Ellis, Varga.

Worth knowing: Brooks and Pruitt are interchangeable at no cost — if you'd rather have a Senate Commerce office than Pruitt, Team A can do Doyle 13:45 → Crowe 14:15 → Brooks 15:15 while Team B does Fischer 13:00 → Abernathy 13:45. Same 76 points. Several of the Tier 3 misses are also one phone call from fitting (e.g., if Grant or Park could do 11:45 Wed, or Nakamura could do 11:30 Tue).

One caveat: I worked this out by hand rather than with a solver, so I can't formally prove 76 is the ceiling — but I checked the main alternative structures (Montoya/Barlow on Tuesday, Fischer on Tuesday, Lindqvist on Tuesday) and they all come out at 74–75, mostly because each one costs Doyle or a Tier 2 office.
